Definition: The last full week, Monday to Sunday. Weekly tiles change on Monday mornings, when a new week closes.
The charts on every page except This Week cover the 12 full weeks up to this week.
Some numbers are a snapshot as at yesterday: backlog, jobs by status, unassigned jobs, open quotes, overdue invoices, overdue Notices of Completion and test and tag due. They move every day.
What a good week looks like. Everyday goals are hit most good weeks; stretch goals are where the business is working to improve.
On target: the goal is met. Watch: close, within a small margin. Off target: further away. A band goal can also be below or above its band.
The best week in the last 12 for that number. The week to beat.
Jobs finished in the week. Callbacks are not counted, because fixing our own work isn't new work.
Every new request for work received in the week, from any source, whether or not it became a job.
Half of the week's enquiries heard back within this time. Clock hours, nights and weekends included, because that is how long the customer waits. An enquiry with no reply yet counts as the slowest.
The share of enquiries that got a first reply within 4 clock hours of arriving.
Of the quotes the customer decided on this week, the share they accepted. Quotes with no decision yet are left out.
The dollar value of quotes accepted and declined in the last 12 weeks, ex GST.
Days from the enquiry arriving to the quote being sent, on average.
Quotes sent with no decision yet, grouped by how many days ago they went out. Over 30 days is stale.
Why declined quotes were lost. 'No reply from customer' is a quote still open after 45 days.
Where the enquiry came from: Google or the website, a referral, a repeat customer, a builder, a property manager, or a lead site.
On-site hours as a share of the hours the field team was available to work. Travel, workshop and paperwork time are not on-site time.
Callbacks booked in the week as a share of jobs completed in the week. A callback is a return visit, at no charge, because the first fix didn't hold.
Value of the week's completed jobs divided by the number of jobs, ex GST.
Invoices past their due date and still unpaid, as at yesterday. A count, not dollars.
Open jobs as at yesterday: booked but not yet scheduled, scheduled, in progress (more visits to come), on hold for parts, or on hold waiting on the customer.
Jobs booked but not yet on anyone's schedule. The office plans five working days ahead, so jobs booked for later dates wait here.
Days of work already booked: the estimated hours still to do on open jobs, divided by about 40 on-site hours a day.
Share of first visits where the electrician arrived within 30 minutes of the booked start time.
How far actual on-site hours ran over (+) or under (-) the estimate, for completed jobs. Hours are person-hours, so an apprentice's time counts too.
Completed jobs in the last 12 weeks by suburb.
Hours come from timesheets: available hours are the rostered hours (7.6 a day), on-site hours are time at jobs, and paid hours include travel, workshop time and overtime.
Travel hours as a share of paid hours for the field team. Time on the road is paid but can't be billed.
Paid hours over the 7.6-hour standard day, added up across the field team.
Job visits led by a licensed electrician, divided by the days they were rostered on. Apprentices work alongside, so they aren't counted.
On-site hours split between licensed electricians (including the owner's days on the tools) and apprentices.
Callbacks booked in the last 12 weeks, counted against the electrician who led the original job, as a share of the jobs they completed.
Completed jobs that needed no unplanned return visit, for example to fit parts that weren't on hand. Planned second visits (rough-in, then fit-off) still count as fixed first time.
The average star rating (1 to 5) from customers who rated a job that week.
Completed jobs that need a Notice of Completion (WA) which hasn't been lodged within 3 days, as at yesterday.
Customers whose next test and tag falls due in the next 30 days, from their most recent test.
Jobs already booked in the old system when the job system went live on 1 Jul 2025.
Tuart Line Electrical is a fictional business. Every number is simulated and updates daily. No real customer data is used.
